messages.subject: Specifying parameter/vector dimensions
parts:
The error is printed during compilation in RStan and occurs when the parameter vector has only one value and is dimensioned in the parameter statement block as "b(1)". 
Successful sampling occurs when instead the parameter(s) is specified with no dimensions ("b") or as "b(2)" in the parameter block.   
Is this really a general restriction on parameter (or vector/matrix) dimensions with the code or am I overlooking something here?
Thanks. 
 
Error : Error during user-specified initialization:
mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context; processing stage=initialization; dims declared=(1); dims found=()
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

parts:
Hi Jiqiang,
This appears to occur after C++ compilation and immediately after this statement:  SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'mod' NOW (CHAIN 1).
 
The vector in question is a parameter vector, to which I've assigned initial values.
One example is betadlv as shown in the parameter statement below.  I finding that if "jjdlv" = 1, the error occurs.  However, if "jjdlv" = 2 or larger values (or if betadlv is not subscripted), the program will execute successfully.
Perhaps this is a standard restriction on vector declarations in C++. 
 
   parameters {        
     real<lower=0,upper=10> betasrc[jjsrc];
     real<lower=0,upper=10> betarch[jjdec];
     real<lower=-10,upper=10> betadlv[jjdlv];
     real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;    
   }
 
Hope that is clearer.
 
btw, I just tried this with another program shown below for a simple linear model (see dimension of parameter "b"), and it produced the same error. 
This is unfortunate as I'd like for my parameter vectors in the other program to be coded in a generic fashion, capable of handling from 1 to n values.
Let me know if there might be an alternative.
 
Thanks for your help.
Richard
 
# multiple-intercept model
radon_code <- '  
   data {    
     int<lower=0> J;         // number of counties    
     int<lower=0> n;         // number of individual radon readings
     real y[n];              // individual radon readings      
     int<lower=0> x[n];      // house level
     int<lower=0> county[n]; //county ID
   }  
   parameters {       
     real mu_a; 
     real b[1];
     real a[J];   
     real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;    
     real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_a; 
   }  
   model {  
    mu_a ~ normal(0,100);       
    sigma_a ~ uniform(0,100);
    a ~ normal(mu_a,sigma_a);        
    b ~ normal(0,100);                
    sigma_y ~ uniform(0,100);
     for (i in 1:n){
      y[i] ~ normal(a[county[i]] + b[1]*x[i],sigma_y);     
     }
   }
 ' 
# END MODEL CODE

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Specifying parameter/vector dimensions
parts:
As there is no scalar in R, it will create some problem for providing data, specifying inits, from RStan to Stan.  
In general, a workaround is to use array with dimension attributes.  So in your non-working R code, the following change would make it work:


## before change 
# Initial values (a function is required)
radon.inits <- function (){
  list ("a"=a,"b"=b,"mu_a"=mu_a,"sigma_y"=sigma_y,"sigma_a"=sigma_a)
}


# after change: 
# Initial values (a function is required)
radon.inits <- function (){
  list ("a"=a,"b"=array(b, dim = length(b)),"mu_a"=mu_a,"sigma_y"=sigma_y,"sigma_a"=sigma_a)
}

Running your code seems to reveal some problem with the plot function in RStan, I will see what is wrong and get it fixed.

--
Jiqiang

list ("a"=a,"b"=array(b, dim = length(b)),"mu_a"=mu_a,"sigma_y"=sigma_y,"sigma_a"=sigma_a)

The problem is R's weak typing and the convention to allow
assignment back and forth.

> a <- 10
> aa <- array(a, dim=length(a))

They print the same way:

> aa
[1] 10
> a
[1] 10

and have the same type:

> typeof(a)
[1] "double"
> typeof(aa)
[1] "double"

and both are is.double():

> is.double(a)
[1] TRUE
> is.double(aa)
[1] TRUE

but is.array() can distinguish them:

> is.array(a)
[1] FALSE
> is.array(aa)
[1] TRUE

but then you can reassign and erase the type again:

> aa <- a

> is.array(aa)
[1] FALSE

Jiqiang --- would it work from the RStan side to just apply this
transform everywhere?

x |-> array(x, dim=length(x))

Or will it fail because now it is an array and not a scalar? I
couldn't even figure out how to test if something's a scalar.
is.double() works for both a and aa. This should all come down
to the implementation of stan::io::var_context for an R environment.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Specifying parameter/vector dimensions
parts:
The real issue is that maybe from the R context, trying
to distinguish scalars from arrays isn't a good idea.

I'd think it'd be possible to implement var_context in such
a way that it can read a scalar from an array or vice-versa
if necessary.

It's sub-optimal from an error checking point of view in case
users confuse types. But given that R itself is fundamentally
confused here, I don't see what else to do other than to have
users do the clunky thing with explicit array constructs (which isn't
actually so bad in my opinion --- this is where some more doc and
a FAQ could help).

- Bob

On Friday, May 17, 2013 5:25:07 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:

being a scalar.  The root reason is that R does not have scalar so there is

This definition of scalar includes lists of length 1, which I don't think should be interpret as scalars in the data block of Stan. I would personally define x as a scalar in R with

is.scalar <- function(x) {
  is.vector(x, mode = "any") && !is.list(x) && length(x) == 1
}
